# FDG3033

> DO NOT introduce overly general type names such as `Element`, `Node`, `Log`, and `Message`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.4.1 Namespaces and Type Name Conflicts.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG3033
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

Message: Qualify the overly general type name '{0}'

FDG3033 reports an externally visible type (any kind, any arity) named exactly Element, Node, Log or Message, the names the rule text lists. Other overly general names are not detected.

## From the book

There is a very high probability that doing so will lead to type name conflicts in common scenarios. You should qualify the general type names (e.g., `FormElement`, `XmlNode`, `EventLog`, `SoapMessage`).

There are specific guidelines for avoiding type name conflicts for different categories of namespaces. Namespaces can be divided into the following categories:

- Application model namespaces
- Infrastructure namespaces
- Core namespaces
- Technology namespace groups
